summary: Falls Point lookout in the Scapegoat Wilderness: a 40-foot L-4 tower burned in the 2012 Falls Point Fire; remains are on the summit.

facts.status_note: Burned in the 2012 Falls Point Fire; remains of the lookout were still on the summit in July 2024.

access.note: On-trail hike in the Scapegoat Wilderness.

visit.trail_note: A well-traveled trail with a 6.4-mile approach from the North Fork trailhead, which has plenty of parking.

events.note: A camp was established at the site.
Firelookout.com says a 40-foot pole L-4 tower was built in 1935. Newspapers of 1935 and 1938 do not confirm this date.
Construction at Falls Point reported under way in September 1938 (Missoulian). Completion date not given.
Burned in the Falls Point Fire of 2012. A dated August 13, 2012 entry says a wildfire consumed the standing ruin.

corrections.why: Both modern accounts give a 40-foot tower, about 12.2 m. 15.2 m is 50 feet, the height a 1938 newspaper gave for the planned towers.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com dates the 40-foot tower to 1935. A 1935 newspaper only names Falls Point as a planned site, and a September 1938 report says construction was under way. The sources do not agree on the year the tower went up; the story reports both.
A 1938 newspaper describes 50-foot towers; firelookout.com and PNW-SOTA describe a 40-foot tower.

notes_for_editor: The firelookout.org index also lists a different Falls Point (Ravalli County, camp abandoned); do not mix it with this site. The CDT article on cdtcoalition.org is about Patrol Mountain, not Falls Point, and is not used. The 1935 vs 1938 build date is unresolved; a Missoulian or Independent Record archive check could settle it. Access 'public' is inferred from the trail descriptions in PNW-SOTA; no closure is described.
